name: Reaching for the Sky
description: From a pharaoh's tomb to Dubai's needle: the structures that each held the record as the tallest thing people had built, one after another, over more than four and a half thousand years.

checkpoints.name: Pyramids and spires
checkpoints.note: Djoser's step pyramid and then the Great Pyramid of Giza made Egypt home to the tallest things on Earth, and the Great Pyramid held the record for nearly four thousand years. The Lighthouse of Alexandria rose high over its harbour, cathedral builders at Chartres raised stone spires, and in 1311 the spire of Lincoln Cathedral finally passed the pyramid.

checkpoints.name: Stone gives way to iron
checkpoints.note: Lincoln's spire fell in 1548, and cathedral builders kept pushing stone upward. Cologne Cathedral, finished in 1880, was briefly the tallest building in the world, until in 1884 the Washington Monument, a plain obelisk of marble and granite, passed it at 169 metres.

checkpoints.name: Steel frames
checkpoints.note: A metal frame in Chicago's Home Insurance Building made tall office blocks possible, and in 1889 the Eiffel Tower, at 300 metres, proved that great height could be a spectacle. Manhattan's Chrysler Building took the title in 1930 and held it for less than a year.

checkpoints.name: The American century
checkpoints.note: The Empire State Building held the record for decades, followed by the World Trade Center, the Willis Tower and Toronto's CN Tower. Then the Petronas Towers carried the contest to Asia.

checkpoints.name: Needles in the east and Gulf
checkpoints.note: Taipei 101 and the Burj Khalifa pushed the record higher in Asia and the Gulf, while Tokyo's Skytree and Shanghai's twisting tower showed how engineers now manage wind, quakes and crowds.
